Discovered by convention alongside ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio's own top-level manifest; merged into one registry, no central edit required.

oracles.rationale:
🩹️ RECLASSIFIED (ticket SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION, shard A10, 2026-09-02). This entry was registered `third-party-library` on the strength of a real crate that does genuine codec work, but the mutation's expected RESULT is computed by this owner's own `🦀️oracle.rs` -- its dispatch function's catch-all arm is `"mutation kind {...} has no oracle implementation"`, proof that every OTHER arm is an implementation, not a reading. Both halves of the comparison then descend from the same specification, so a shared misreading produces two agreeing wrong answers -- the one failure a differential oracle exists to catch. This is a `cross-semio-implementation`: a required SUPPLEMENT (metamorphic/inverse/round-trip evidence), never a substitute. A qualifying third-party reference for the mutation semantics is still owed. See $TICKET/📓️a10-oracle-honesty.md.

A PPTX is a ZIP of XML parts (ECMA-376 Part 2 OPC). No standalone `pptx` crate is registered: the only one on crates.io is a 0.1.0 first release, and a first-release crate judging our implementation would be worse than none (fleet brief instruction). `zip` and `quick-xml` are both already linked for other subsets (🎒zip, 📰xml, 🎨svg) and both genuinely independent of this repository's own PPTX codec — this oracle unzips with `zip`, parses/edits/re-serializes `ppt/presentation.xml` and every `ppt/slides/slideN.xml` with `quick-xml`, and rezips with `zip`. Every mutation kind is expressed as a pure operation on an independent, typed, ordered slide/shape list, then EVERY slide-related OPC part (slides, their `.rels`, `presentation.xml`'s `p:sldIdLst`, `presentation.xml.rels`'s slide relationships, `[Content_Types].xml`'s slide `Override`s) is freshly regenerated from that list — a genuine re-serialization on every call, never a byte pass-through, including `no-mutation` and `identity-round-trip`.

packages.role: independent XML reader/writer for every part inside the archive

comparisonProfiles.description: PPTX presentations compared as an ORDERED list of slides (slide order is part of the model — `move-slide` is the whole point of this vocabulary), each an ORDERED list of shapes, each shape's kind/text/position. Both producers' projections are re-derived from raw OPC/XML bytes by the SAME independent `zip`+`quick-xml` reader (never trusted from either producer's own typed model), scoped to exactly what `crate::artifacts::pptx::schema::snapshot::PptxShape` itself models: shape kind (textBox/placeholder/picture/other), a placeholder's own `phKind`, a shape's text content (paragraph boundaries joined by newline — per-run bold/italic/font-size styling is writer freedom, not normative here), and its `a:xfrm` position in EMUs (a shape with no explicit `a:xfrm`, inheriting its position from the slide layout, projects as x=y=cx=cy=0 on both sides — the same default `crate::artifacts::pptx`'s own importer uses for a missing `a:xfrm`). OPC-level plumbing a rebuilt slide mints fresh on every call — slide/shape XML part paths, relationship ids, `p:sldId`'s numeric `id`, `p:cNvPr`'s shape id/name, which slideLayout a rebuilt slide targets — is deliberately absent from the projection because `PptxSnapshot`'s own typed model does not track it either; it is OPC packaging freedom, not shape content.
